messages.subject: right truncation of data
parts:
Hi All,

I'm using gdistsamp to model small mammal density at point counts taken over multiple visits. My points are along  line transects, and are 333m apart.  In an effort to reduce double-counting and non-independence between points, I was planning to truncate the data from each point at 167m.  This truncates about 50% of the data, however, and produces a different key function as the best fitting model; if truncated, an exponential fits best, if not, a half-normal. I also get very different densities from the two models. Using backTransform(null, type="lambda"), I get 76 per km2 from the truncated data, and 30 per km2 from untruncated data. I know that truncating the top 5% of the data is the usual procedure, but can anyone tell me whether too much truncation causes problems? Would I be better to truncate at 300 m, which includes 95% of the data?  I expected the detection function to be the same for a given dataset, but maybe I'm not thinking about it correctly.  

Thanks so much for your help,

Lucretia

messages.author: 4a15de51da4445ae
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] right truncation of data
parts:
I would guess that the two models are very sensitive to the tail of the distance distribution, so throwing out the furthest 50% of the observations should have a huge impact on the fit of those two models I think.
I think people who do distance sampling say to avoid the exponential model for various reasons. Sensitivity of estimates, doesn't have a shoulder, ... I don't really know the particulars on that.
regards
andy
